subject: Holiday Campaign Creative — Final Concept
snippet: Team, We need to land the final creative concept for the holiday campaign this week so Fold & Field has enough runway to produce everything before BFCM. I've been sitting with the
body_text:
Team,

We need to land the final creative concept for the holiday campaign this week so Fold & Field has enough runway to produce everything before BFCM. I've been sitting with the three directions from last week's review and want to lay out where my head is, but I want real pushback if you disagree — this decision is expensive to unwind once production starts.

DIRECTION A — 'Gathered' (the minimalist, editorial one): clean product shots on neutral backgrounds, heavy whitespace, very restrained typography. Pros: cheapest to produce, fastest turnaround, on-brand with our spring campaign so there's visual continuity. Cons: doesn't feel very 'holiday,' risk of blending into the crowded promo inbox in November.

DIRECTION B — 'Warm Nights' (the lifestyle one): full sets built out as cozy living rooms and dining scenes, warm lighting, models, the whole thing. This is the one that tested best in the June concept survey — respondents specifically called out feeling 'want to be in that room.' Pros: strongest emotional pull, most differentiated from competitors who are all doing clean minimalist holiday campaigns this year. Cons: expensive — full set builds, casting, multi-day shoot — and the most schedule risk given how tight our September production window already is.

DIRECTION C — 'Gift Guide First' (the utility one): leads with gifting categories and price points rather than mood, closer to what Denise's ecommerce team wants for conversion. Pros: cheapest, fastest, plays well with paid social direct-response ads. Cons: least brand-building, feels more like a retailer than Habitat Goods.

Budget envelope for creative production is roughly $85K regardless of which direction we pick — that number doesn't flex much either way.

One more thing worth naming: last year we made this exact call in late September, which left almost no cushion when the set builder ran two weeks over on the winter cabin concept. I don't want to repeat that. If we're doing B, I need everyone's honest read on schedule risk now, not a polite 'sure, sounds doable' that turns into a September fire drill. If the honest answer is that B is too tight given everything else on the calendar (the replatform QA window, the Amara whitelisting campaign, PR's Business Insider push), I'd rather hear that today and fall back to A or C than find out in three weeks.

I want to make the call by end of week. Please reply with your honest take by Friday — Rachel, especially want your read on production feasibility for B given the timeline; Cam, how each direction supports the content calendar; Tessa, ballpark cost delta between B and the other two if you have it offhand.

Thanks all,
Sofia

subject: Q4 Planning Priorities
snippet: Jordan, As we head into the last full planning push before Q4, wanted to put in writing where I think our priorities need to sit so we're aligned before you build out the departmen
body_text:
Jordan,

As we head into the last full planning push before Q4, wanted to put in writing where I think our priorities need to sit so we're aligned before you build out the department OKRs.

1. HOLIDAY CAMPAIGN — this is the single biggest lever we have this quarter. Between the creative direction (still being finalized, I know) and the media plan, I want this locked with zero ambiguity by the first week of September. BFCM is non-negotiable — we cannot repeat last year's late-approval scramble where the agency was still turning around assets 4 days before launch.

2. RETENTION / LIFECYCLE — Ben's abandoned cart and post-purchase flow work has been quietly good this year, and I think there's real headroom left. I'd like a proposal from you on whether we invest further here in Q4 or hold steady and focus resources on acquisition given the holiday push. Genuinely open on this one, want your read.

3. WEBSITE REPLATFORM — launch date has already moved once (now Aug 17 per Nina), and the timing is uncomfortably close to when we need go-to-market assets locked for holiday. Want a contingency plan in case it slips again — what does the campaign look like if we're still running on the old site template through the holiday launch?

4. AGENCY RELATIONSHIP — the Fold & Field retainer renewal needs to close out before Q1, and given how much production load is shifting onto them for the holiday campaign, I want to make sure the new scope actually reflects what we're asking them to do, not just a rubber-stamp of last year's terms.

5. BUDGET DISCIPLINE — finance has been clear that overall marketing spend needs to flex with margin pressure this quarter (you saw Wes's note on paid social). I'd rather we get ahead of this proactively department-wide than have individual budget lines get cut reactively in November.

None of this is meant to be exhaustive — I know you've got your own read on priorities too, and I want this to be a conversation, not a directive. Let's grab 45 minutes this week to talk through it before you finalize the OKR doc. I'd like to review a draft before it goes to the broader team, ideally by August 21st so we have runway to socialize it before the offsite.

Thanks for everything you're carrying right now — I know Q4 planning season is a lot on top of the day-to-day.

Sofia

meta.action_summary: Jordan needs to draft the Q4 department OKRs incorporating Sofia's five priorities and get a draft to Sofia by August 21st.

subject: Content Calendar — Q4 Editorial Strategy
snippet: Jordan, Wanted to get you the full Q4 editorial strategy before our sync Friday so you have time to react. Here's where my head's at. BLOG: Shifting from our current 2x/week genera
body_text:
Jordan,

Wanted to get you the full Q4 editorial strategy before our sync Friday so you have time to react. Here's where my head's at.

BLOG: Shifting from our current 2x/week general lifestyle cadence to a themed-month structure — September is 'Small Space Solutions' (ties to the back-to-school apartment-furnishing traffic we see every year), October is 'Hosting Season' (leads naturally into the holiday gifting push), November-December is full gift-guide mode with weekly refreshes based on inventory and what's trending in paid social. This gives us a clearer narrative thread than the somewhat scattered approach we've had, and lets SEO content compound instead of competing with itself across too many topics at once.

EMAIL/SMS EDITORIAL SUPPORT: Coordinating closely with Ben on lifecycle so editorial content (styling guides, care tips, behind-the-scenes sourcing stories) feeds directly into flows rather than living only on the blog. The reclaimed-wood sourcing story specifically tested really well as email content in the spring — I want three more pieces in that same 'origin story' format for Q4, likely tied to the holiday campaign's Direction B lifestyle sets — or Direction C now, I saw the thread.

SOCIAL: Leaning further into UGC given how well the TikTok creative refresh performed in Q3 (Nina's recap has the numbers — CAC and ROAS both meaningfully better than our produced content). Want to formalize a small UGC budget line separate from the paid whitelisting spend so we're not treating it as an afterthought.

PR TIE-INS: Priyanka's team has three placements in the pipeline for Q4 (Business Insider ran, two more pending) and I want blog/social content ready to amplify each one within 24 hours of publication rather than the usual week-later scramble.

HEADCOUNT: Flagging early — if we add the UGC program and the origin-story email series on top of the existing blog cadence, I think I need either a part-time contractor or a shift in my own priorities. Not asking for a decision now, just want it on your radar before Q4 actually starts.

MEASUREMENT: One thing I want to fix from last quarter — we never agreed on what 'working' means for the blog beyond raw sessions. Proposing we track assisted conversions from blog-sourced sessions specifically, plus email signups attributed to content, so we're not just reporting traffic that doesn't tie back to anything Sofia or finance cares about. I can pull last year's numbers as a baseline if that's useful before Friday.

TIMELINE RISK: The themed-month structure only works if September content is locked by August 22nd at the latest — anything later and we lose the back-to-school traffic window entirely, since that search demand falls off a cliff after Labor Day. I'd rather flag that constraint now than discover it the week we're supposed to publish.

Let me know if any of this conflicts with where you and Sofia are landing on overall priorities — happy to adjust before Friday.

Cam
